data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'l-w-k' meaning 'to be lofty, exalted, or divine'. In Islamic spiritual traditions, Malayeka refers to a divine creature or angel, often associated with grace, kindness, and purity. The name Malayeka carries the meaning “Angelic, Divine Creature” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Malayeka usually hope their child will grow to embody angelic, divine creature and live with faith, good character and purpose.
